# Repository instructions

## Build, test, and lint

This is a Rust 2024 crate with minimum supported Rust 1.88. CI runs on Linux and
macOS with both stable Rust and Rust 1.88. Runtime use requires OpenSSH.

Run commands from the repository root:

```sh
cargo build --locked
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --all-targets --locked
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --locked
```

The formatting, Clippy, test, and documentation commands match
[CI](workflows/ci.yml). To run one integration-test file or one test:

```sh
cargo test --locked --test topology
cargo test --locked --test topology direct_alias_pattern_and_ipv6_endpoints -- --exact
```

Public API documentation is linted; unsafe code is forbidden. Preserve Rust 1.88
compatibility when changing APIs or dependencies.

## Architecture

sshweave generates OpenSSH configuration and supplies its ProxyCommand transport;
OpenSSH remains responsible for SSH itself.

- [config](../src/config.rs) loads and validates TOML, includes, templates, and
  inheritance. [resolver](../src/resolver.rs) turns a requested target into a
  `ResolvedHost`, including transport and gateway choices.
- [render](../src/render.rs) translates resolved hosts into OpenSSH configuration.
  [store](../src/store.rs) persists that configuration and a registry of
  materialized targets and gateways. The registry is not an SSH known-hosts file
  or credential store.
- [runtime](../src/runtime.rs) implements the ProxyCommand byte stream through
  direct TCP, HTTP/SOCKS5 proxies, local commands, and SSH gateways.
  [proxy](../src/proxy.rs) handles proxy endpoint parsing and handshakes;
  [hooks](../src/hooks.rs) handles lifecycle commands.
- [topology](../src/topology.rs) expands routes for preview without connecting,
  running commands or hooks, or writing files.
  [sockets](../src/sockets.rs) manages OpenSSH control sockets.

For configuration syntax, CLI usage, hook templates, and worked routing examples,
see the [main README](../README.md), [detailed examples](../examples/README.md),
and [sample configuration](../examples/sshweave.toml). Chinese counterparts are
[README_CN](../README_CN.md) and [examples/README_CN](../examples/README_CN.md).

## Repository-specific conventions

- Relative configuration paths resolve from the TOML file's directory.
  `$HOME/.config/sshweave/conf.d/*.toml` is automatically loaded. Integration
  tests isolate `HOME` through [tests/common](../tests/common/mod.rs); preserve
  that isolation instead of reading the developer's configuration.
- Rendering must stay deterministic. Emit concrete hosts before wildcard rules,
  and exclude materialized hosts from wildcard rules so OpenSSH does not
  accumulate options from both.
- Generated configuration starts with `# Generated by sshweave; DO NOT EDIT.`.
  Synchronization refuses to replace unmarked files and runs config-write hooks
  only when content changes. Preserve exclusive locking, `0600` permissions,
  fsync, atomic replacement, and directory fsync in persistence changes.
- ProxyCommand stdout carries SSH protocol bytes. Diagnostics and hook output
  belong on stderr. Hook templates use strict MiniJinja undefined-variable
  handling; use the `shellquote` filter when inserting values into shell commands.
  Hooks are trusted executable configuration.
- `on_connect` means transport establishment, not successful SSH authentication.
  `on_disconnect` follows the proxy stream, not each multiplexed SSH session.
  Runtime transport changes must preserve the destination-first-byte probe and
  bidirectional streaming with half-close support.
- Preserve nested-route safeguards: `SSHWEAVE_ROUTE_STACK` detects cycles,
  `SSHWEAVE_ROUTE_PROXY` forces the outermost proxy, and gateway recursion is
  bounded at 32. A transport cannot combine a proxy with `proxy_command`.
  Current HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy support is unauthenticated.
- Keep topology previews side-effect-free and retain their 4096-node expansion
  limit as well as gateway depth/cycle checks.
- Integration tests use local TCP and controlled proxy processes rather than
  external SSH servers or credentials. Transport behavior is covered in
  [transport tests](../tests/transport.rs) and [proxy tests](../tests/proxy.rs);
  resolution/rendering behavior is covered in
  [configuration tests](../tests/configuration.rs) and
  [topology tests](../tests/topology.rs).
